site-tenant-accent.displayName: Tenant Accent (runtime; configPadrao default: a rose)

site-tenant-accent-deep.displayName: Tenant Accent, Deep (runtime; the site's full-fill background)

painel-display.purpose: Headlines, stat numbers, wizard title — the 'headline' number, not the 'coordinate' number.

painel-mono.purpose: Times, log timestamps, slot labels — any scannable number.

vital-body.purpose: All text. Replaced Inter this pass — a deliberate identity decision (shares an origin with the audit-trail mono, and Inter was flagged as an unexamined default), not the earlier bug fix that only added the missing @import.

vital-mono.purpose: Audit-trail action label. Now the same type family as vital-body.

site-body.purpose: All text including headings; hierarchy from size/weight/tracking, not a font pairing. Replaced Inter this pass to keep the single-family system while losing the generic-default read.

site-rotulo.purpose: Smallest uppercase labels: weekday header, summary label, item captions.

site-legenda.purpose: Meta/caption text: field labels, struck-through prices, footnotes.

site-auxiliar.purpose: Secondary body: helper copy, descriptions, guide-column paragraphs.

site-corpo-pq.purpose: Small UI text: most button/label/value text that isn't the primary name.

site-corpo.purpose: Primary names: service name, option name, slogan, header brand name.

site-titulo-pq.purpose: Sub-headings: guide-column step name, month name, promo name.

site-titulo.purpose: Step titles: booking-window header, category name, confirmation heading.

site-destaque.purpose: The one emphasized number on the page: a promo's discounted price.

site-secao.purpose: Section titles: company name, 'Nossos serviços'-style headings.

site-hero.purpose: The largest mark on the page: logo initial, service-circle initial.

shadows.name: site-ambient
shadows.purpose: Ownerless ambient light — booking window, header logo mark. No implied direction.

shadows.name: site-bandeja
shadows.purpose: Directional light, brand-ink tinted — service circles and promo cards at rest/hover-start. Part of the 'A Bandeja' thesis: each service is an object on a lit tray, not an icon floating in space.

shadows.name: site-bandeja-hover
shadows.purpose: Same light, closer — the object lifts off the tray on hover.

shadows.name: site-window
shadows.purpose: The booking window, the only modal-scale surface on site.

shadows.name: painel-sticky
shadows.purpose: The sticky config-save bar and toast.

shadows.name: vital-none
shadows.purpose: Vital uses no shadow vocabulary at rest or floating — depth is a border + surface-step relationship only. See DESIGN.md Elevation & Depth.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Shared instinct across all three systems for hover/press/focus transitions — short, no bounce, no scale.

motion.name: site-cover-zoom
motion.purpose: Slow zoom-in on the site's cover photo on first paint, not scroll-driven.

motion.name: site-reveal
motion.value: .55s ease/cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1), translateY(18px) to none, opacity 0 to 1
motion.purpose: Scroll-reveal on site sections; fully disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

components.name: Site — Primary Button
components.description: Pill button using the site's full-fill pair — shown here with the system default; the real value is injected per tenant at runtime. Hover is a brightness filter on the same fill, not a second computed color.

narrative.overview:
Vital is not one interface wearing three skins — it is three coherent, independently-evolved visual systems, each serving a public that never sees the other two. The product's own architecture forces this: site, painel and vital.html are separate Vite bundles, separate CSS files, separate audiences, and the codebase already gives two of the three systems descriptive token names (porcelain, lacquer, blush, ink) that read like they were designed on purpose, not defaulted into.

Two of the three are ledgers — fixed, opinionated, unapologetically branded design languages that exist regardless of which tenant is using the product. The Atelier Ledger (painel) is warm, serif-headlined, porcelain-and-lacquer, built for a person who opens it fifty times a day from a phone at the counter. The Plain Ledger (vital.html) is the same record-keeping instinct with the warmth stripped out — purple, IBM Plex Sans paired with the IBM Plex Mono of its own audit trail, mostly borders, because this is where the Vital team administers other people's businesses and the tone is administrative trust, not hospitality.

The third is The Blank Canvas (site) — the one system in the product whose primary color is not a design decision at all. --marca arrives at runtime from the tenant's own config; the system's real signature is everything that doesn't change: the pill-shaped buttons, the circular photo grid, the 14px corner radius, the slow zoom-in on the cover photo, and now Manrope carrying that warmth in type instead of the Inter it shipped with. Site is the only surface designed to be worn by a color it doesn't choose.

Within that canvas, site's composition now carries a second, more specific thesis: A Bandeja (the tray). Mood-referenced from a real neighborhood esthetics studio's Instagram rather than the category's own cliché (cream ground, elegant serif, gold accent), each service reads as an object resting on a lit surface, not an icon on a card. The header no longer depends on a cover photo for impact — it didn't have one in the environment this was built in, and needed to work without one first — and the service circles carry a directional, brand-ink-tinted shadow instead of the system's ambient one.
keyCharacteristics: Three separate token vocabularies, never shared, never crossing bundle boundaries
Two fixed brands (painel, Vital) built for operators; one adaptive shell (site) built to disappear behind whichever tenant is using it
lucide-react is the one true cross-cutting convention across all three bundles
Componentry is refined and comedido everywhere — short transitions, no scale/bounce, shallow functional shadow
No system uses Inter — painel (Fraunces/Karla), Vital (IBM Plex Sans/Mono) and site (Manrope) each committed to a face Inter's ubiquity doesn't carry

rules.name: The Named-Twin Rule
rules.body: --p-marca, --p-escuro and --p-linha in painel are exact aliases of --lacquer, --ink and --line — not a second palette.

rules.name: The Unused-Token Rule
rules.body: --gold in painel is declared and never used. Give it a real job before designing with it.

rules.name: The Injectable-Accent Rule
rules.body: Site's tenant-accent tokens are runtime data, not design constants — never hardcode a specific hex for 'the site's brand color'.

rules.name: The Muted-Text Floor
rules.body: painel's --muted and site's --fraco were both darkened once already to clear WCAG AA (4.42:1 to 4.77:1, and 2.81:1 to 4.74:1). Don't re-lighten either without re-checking contrast against every background it's used on.

rules.name: The Two-Number Rule
rules.body: In painel, set a number in Fraunces when it's a headline and in IBM Plex Mono when it's a coordinate someone scans against others.

rules.name: The One-Plex Rule
rules.body: Vital's body and mono are both IBM Plex now. Don't introduce a third, unrelated family for a new role — extend within Plex Sans's weight range first.

rules.name: The One-Family Rule
rules.body: Site deliberately uses Manrope alone, for every role. Don't add a second family for 'more personality' — the tenant's injected accent color is where per-client personality already lives.

rules.name: The Float-Only-Shadow Rule
rules.body: On site and painel, shadow appears only on elements that float above the base layer (modals, sticky bars, toasts, photo circles). A card at rest never carries one. Vital carries none at all, ever.

rules.name: The On-Accent-Deep Rule
rules.body: Every solid-fill surface on site (primary button, Destaque, selos, selected states, the confirmation mark) uses --marca-escura background with --sobre-marca-escura text, never the plain --marca/--sobre-marca pair. --marca-escura is not a fixed -25% shade — paraTextoBranco() darkens the tenant color only as far as it takes for the color itself to hold white at >=4.5:1, so an already-dark accent (most blues, greens) comes back nearly unchanged, while a light one (a sage, a pastel) darkens for real. Never assume a derived shade inherits its base color's on-top text choice; --sobre-marca-escura is its own contraste() call.

rules.name: The Sixteen-Sixty Rule
rules.body: --t-corpo-gr (16px) is a token; the literal 16px forced onto every real <input>/<select>/<textarea> is not, on purpose — that number exists to stop iOS auto-zoom, not to express hierarchy, and tying it to a retunable token would silently reopen that bug.

rules.name: The Rhythm-Isn't-Sizing Rule
rules.body: Site's nine-step spacing scale (--e-1 4px through --e-9 52px) covers rhythm between elements. Touch targets (40/44/46/48/56/64px min-height) stay literal on purpose — they're an accessibility constant, not a statement about air between things.

rules.name: The No-Photo-Required Rule
rules.body: Site's header composition must look finished with zero uploaded images — no tenant in this product's dev environment has one. The header's typographic treatment is identical whether marca.capa exists or not; a cover photo, when present, renders as a strip above the header, never as its load-bearing backdrop.

rules.name: The Bandeja-Shadow Rule
rules.body: --sombra-bandeja / --sombra-bandeja-hover are directional and brand-ink-tinted, reserved for the service-circle/promo-card 'object on a tray' material. --sombra stays the system's ownerless ambient shadow for everything else that floats. Don't swap one for the other as a generic strength dial.

rules.name: The One-Fill-Doesn't-Repeat-Everywhere Rule
rules.body: .bloco-cheio (a full-bleed section in the full-fill accent pair, used on Clinica's 'Quem cuida de voce' and footer) is opt-in per section, not a model-wide background swap. Clinica earned it because its own neutrals are white/light-gray throughout and read as all-white without at least one true full-color section; the other three models don't share that problem and weren't asked for it.

dos: Do keep the three token vocabularies fully separate — a decision made for one surface carries no default authority over the other two.
Do treat --marca and its derived shades on site as runtime data, always with a static fallback for pre-hydration paint.
Do use --sobre-marca-escura, not --sobre-marca, for text on any surface colored with --marca-escura.

Do use the --marca-escura/--sobre-marca-escura pair, not --marca/--sobre-marca, for any new solid-fill site surface (a filled button, a filled badge, a selected state); reserve the plain pair for a thin accent that was never going to hold text at its own intensity.
Do reach for site's --t-* and --e-* tokens first for new site typography or spacing; a new literal should be the exception, not the default.
Do use IBM Plex Mono for any new scannable number on painel or Vital; use the surface's display or body font for headline numbers.
Do keep shadow reserved for floating elements on site and painel, and keep Vital flat.
Do use lucide-react, inline, for any new icon in any of the three bundles.
donts: Don't reuse painel's --lacquer value for Vital's accent or vice versa — they're independently-maintained tokens that happen to be close today.
Don't give a Vital button or card a pill radius or a drop shadow — both are confirmed painel/site signatures Vital doesn't share.
Don't re-lighten painel's --muted or site's --fraco without re-checking WCAG contrast — both were corrected once already to clear AA.
Don't assume painel or Vital have a spacing scale — they still don't, on purpose; only site does now.
Don't fold site's touch-target min-heights (40/44/46/48/56/64px) into the --e-* spacing scale — they're accessibility constants, not rhythm.
Don't repeat painel's .btn-wa hardcoded WhatsApp-green pattern for anything other than an actual WhatsApp affordance.
Don't reach for Inter, Roboto, Geist, Plus Jakarta Sans, or Space Grotesk as a default for a new surface — none of the three existing systems uses any of them, on purpose.
